notes: Unqualified droop -> RACE facial 2 (§4); positive RACE finding also a deficit (§4b); G.F.A.S.T. before RACE (§5a); husband's LKW clause only is family (§3).
Drift -> RACE arm 1, G.F.A.S.T. arm_leg 1, deficit (§4, §4d). Anticoagulant before meds.list for one drug word (§5b).
Slurred = dysarthria: G.F.A.S.T. speech 1, no RACE aphasia (§5a). Plavix is an antiplatelet: meds.list only (§5a). 'She takes' said by medic with no attribution -> medic (§3, §5b).

Woke up with it / nobody saw it -> onset_witnessed false (§4, §5b); stroke dispatch so labeled without a named symptom (§4c). 'This morning' wake-up is a discovery time, no time fact (§4c, §5b). Bedtime 'at 10 last night' -> '10 pm' (§4c).
Can't speak -> RACE aphasia 2 (§4) and G.F.A.S.T. speech 1 (§4d). Both deficits in one list fact (my convention: one list fact per key per utterance).

'Keeps using the wrong words' read as word-finding/language trouble with no severity: G.F.A.S.T. speech 1 + deficit, no RACE aphasia value (§5b). 'Face even, no droop' -> facial 0 on both scales, no deficit (§4b, §4d).
Medic-spoken RACE item scores map to G.F.A.S.T. (§4d); bare RACE scores give no deficits (§5b). 'Her son saw it happen': source is the person named -> family (§5b 'last seen normal by her daughter').
'GFAST positive, all four' -> all four items 1 (§4d), no deficits (§5b). 'This morning' adds am (§5b). Husband's explicit denial -> anticoagulant none, family (§4).
'By mouth' -> route PO (§4e).
symptom.onset keeps 'since', 'this morning' adds am (§5b). 'She tells me' -> patient (§3). No 12-lead time was said.
Patient's own nitro before arrival -> meds.list, not meds.given (§4b, §4e). Transmitted gives only ecg.transmitted (no time, not 'attached') (§4, §4e).
Two nitro doses with no separate times -> one fact with count 2 (§4e). Under the tongue -> SL.

facts: tripped on the rug and fell
notes: Mechanism counts as complaint and as trauma.mechanism (§4, §4e). No height/head impact -> no trauma.criteria (§4e). Anticoagulant never goes in criteria (§4e).

No seatbelt + rollover -> 'rollover unrestrained'; thrown from the car -> 'ejection' (§4e). GCS components only, no computed total (§4e); no ACVPU from GCS numbers (§4c). Assumed the driver is the patient.

facts: stab wound to the upper left thigh
stab wound to the upper left thigh
penetrating injury head neck torso or proximal extremity
bleeding requiring tourniquet or wound packing
notes: Penetrating wound gives complaint, mechanism and injury (§4e). Upper thigh read as proximal extremity (proximal to the knee) -> penetrating criterion. Tourniquet -> bleeding criterion (§4e example). Both criteria in one list fact (my convention).

facts: fall from 12 feet off a roof
obvious deformity of the right wrist
notes: 'About 12 feet': approximator dropped, not a hedge -> fall over 10 feet (§4e). Wrist deformity alone not labeled as 'time sensitive extremity injury' (no open fracture/neurovascular loss stated).

facts: pedestrian hit by a car, thrown 20 feet
pedestrian or cyclist thrown or run over
notes: 'Unstable pelvis' -> injury + 'pelvic fracture' criterion (§4e example). Vital-sign criteria (SBP, GCS) never go in trauma.criteria (§4e). Both criteria in one list fact (my convention).
Nursing-home nurse is facility staff -> family (§3, §5b). Being treated for UTI -> source 'urinary' (§4e). 102.4 F -> 39.1 C (§4). No complaint.chief: the UTI is held by infection.suspected (§4c).
New confusion -> C, not a complaint (§4, §4c). 'Looks like pneumonia' -> respiratory (§4e).

Infected foot wound -> infection.suspected skin (§4e example); not labeled trauma.injuries (sepsis call, infected wound is not an injury found after trauma) and no separate complaint.chief (held by infection.suspected, §4c). 'Temp 100.9' has no unit said; only Fahrenheit is plausible -> 38.3 C (§4).
'Found him confused' -> C; hypoglycemia, so no stroke.onset_witnessed (§4c). D10 -> dextrose (§4e). Recheck -> second glucose and consciousness facts, not corrections (§4b, §4c).

Read 'his roommate says he sprayed one dose of Narcan up his nose' as the roommate giving it -> meds.given by bystander (roommate is a bystander synonym), role bystander (§3, §4e). 'One dose' -> no count field (count is for multiple doses, §4e). Fire's dose reported by the medic without 'fire says' -> role medic, by fire (§4e). Non-rebreather -> on_oxygen true (§4).

Mom's clause -> family for complaint and onset time (§3, §4c). Seizure clock time -> symptom.onset '3:10' (no am/pm said). Duration 'about 2 minutes' has no key. 'She takes Keppra' is a new clause -> medic (§4c).
'Can't catch her breath' said by the medic unattributed -> complaint.chief, role medic (§3, §4).
Wife on the mic -> family for everything (§3, §5a). Family's description of a droop -> deficit only, no RACE/G.F.A.S.T. (§4d, §5b).

'A water pill' is a class with no name -> not in meds.list (§4c). No sex label from 'Mom' (kinship word treated like a pronoun, not a descriptor, §4 patient.sex). Low fall with no head impact -> no trauma.criteria (§4e).
Patient on the mic -> patient role (§3). 'About' dropped (§4c). Brilinta is an antiplatelet: no anticoagulant (§5a).

Dispatch is 'unknown problem', but the utterance describes stroke-like symptoms (limp arm, can't talk), so stroke keys are labeled (§4c). 'Found her' -> onset_witnessed false (§5b); 'this morning' is a discovery time, no fact (§5b). LKW '5 pm yesterday' written '5 pm' (§4c 'last night' pattern drops the day word). Neighbor's description -> deficits only, no RACE/G.F.A.S.T. (§5b). No scene.notes/complaint for 'on the kitchen floor' (found down is not a mechanism, §4e).

Patient's own insulin dose reported by husband stays meds.list (§4e). Home-meter glucose from husband -> family. Glucose gel the husband gave -> meds.given drug 'glucose', by family (§4e); 'a tube' is not a unit and route not said, so dose/unit/route left empty.

'Not on any blood thinners anymore' is an explicit denial -> none; stopped Xarelto gets no meds.list (§5b). Neighbor relayed by son -> bystander (§4b nested attribution). No sex label from 'Dad' (same call as fc26).
